title: Which carbon scheme touches you, and what changes in 2028?
sub: NI firms, councils and operators. UK–EU link agreed 20 November 2026, aiming for 2028; not yet law.
note: NI generators stay in the EU ETS under the Windsor Framework; other NI installations are in the UK ETS. NI energy-from-waste treatment is unclear in the government explainer. Status 21 November 2026. Not legal or tax advice.
nodes: Your NI business, council or operation
start
Do you generate electricity for the all-island market?
q
EU ETS stays. From 2028 UK and EU allowances count in both.
out
Do you run a UK ETS installation (combustion over 20 MW or a listed activity)?
q
No price floor, EU free-allocation rules, prices converge.
warn
Do you run ships of 5,000 GT or more on UK routes?
q
GB–NI 50% discount ends; half of international voyages covered.
pay
Do you operate flights from the UK?
q
One-stop shop for airlines in both schemes; no CORSIA on flights to the EEA.
out
Do you run or pay for energy-from-waste?
q
Monitoring from 2028 in GB; paying later. NI unclear.
warn
Do you trade CBAM goods with the EU?
q
UK exempts EU goods (intended 2027); EU exempts UK goods (expected 2028).
out
Indirect effects only: freight, power and supplier prices.
